name: Task format
desc:
The format that Tasks uses to read and write tasks.

Important: Tasks currently only supports one format at a time. Selecting Dataview will currently stop Tasks reading its own emoji signifiers.

Reload Obsidian to apply this change.

See the documentation

name: Global filter
desc:
Recommended: Leave empty if you want all checklist items in your vault to be tasks managed by this plugin.

Use a global filter if you want Tasks to only act on a subset of your "- [ ]" checklist items, so that a checklist item must include the specified string in its description in order to be considered a task.

For example, if you set the global filter to #task, the Tasks plugin will only handle checklist items tagged with #task. Other checklist items will remain normal checklist items and not appear in queries or get a done date set.

See the documentation

name: Remove global filter from description
desc:
Enabling this removes the string that you set as global filter from the task description when displaying a task.

Reload Obsidian to apply this change.

name: Task statuses
desc:
Core statuses

These are the core statuses that Tasks supports natively, with no need for custom CSS styling or theming.

Custom statuses

You can add and edit your own custom statuses in the Custom statuses section.

You should first select and install a CSS snippet or theme to style custom checkboxes. Then, set up your custom statuses to match your chosen CSS checkboxes.

See the documentation to get started!

name: Global query
desc:
Instructions automatically included at the start of every Tasks block.

See the documentation

You can define named instructions here, that you can re-use in multiple queries. A preset called 'name' can be used in Tasks queries with either 'preset name' or '{{preset.name}}'.

Any open Tasks queries are reloaded automatically when presets are edited.

See the documentation

name: Enable custom searches
desc:
Enables 'filter by function', 'sort by function', and 'group by function', which execute JavaScript in Tasks queries.

Malicious JavaScript in a Tasks query or Markdown file could run inside Obsidian and access or modify your vault contents, local files, or other system resources.

Only enable this if you trust the current and future contents of this vault, including files you may later download, copy, or sync from other people.

This setting is stored on this device only; enable it separately on each device where you use this vault.

See the documentation

name: Set created date on every added task
desc:
Enabling this will add a timestamp ➕ YYYY-MM-DD before other date values, when a task is created with 'Create or edit task', or by completing a recurring task.

See the documentation

name: Set done date on every completed task
desc:
Enabling this will add a timestamp ✅ YYYY-MM-DD at the end when a task is toggled to done.

See the documentation

name: Set cancelled date on every cancelled task
desc:
Enabling this will add a timestamp ❌ YYYY-MM-DD at the end when a task is toggled to cancelled.

See the documentation

name: Use filename as Scheduled date for undated tasks
desc:
Save time entering Scheduled (⏳) dates. If this option is enabled, any undated tasks will be given a default Scheduled date extracted from their file name.

By default, Tasks plugin will match both YYYY-MM-DD and YYYYMMDD date formats. Undated tasks have none of Due (📅 ), Scheduled (⏳) and Start (🛫) dates.

Reload Obsidian to apply this change.

See the documentation

name: Additional filename date format as Scheduled date for undated tasks
desc:
An additional date format that Tasks plugin will recogize when using the file name as the Scheduled date for undated tasks.

Reload Obsidian to apply this change.

See the documentation

name: Folders with default Scheduled dates
desc:
Leave empty if you want to use default Scheduled dates everywhere, or enter a comma-separated list of folders.

Reload Obsidian to apply this change.

name: Next recurrence appears on the line below
desc:
Enabling this will make the next recurrence of a task appear on the line below the completed task. Otherwise the next recurrence will appear before the completed one.

See the documentation

name: Remove scheduled date on recurrence
desc:
Enabling this will make the next recurrence of a task have no Scheduled (⏳) date, when at least one of Start (🛫) or Due (📅) dates is present.

This is for when you want the Start and Due dates to carry forward to the next recurrence, but you will set the Scheduled date in future, once you plan to work on it.

See the documentation

name: Auto-suggest task content
desc:
Enabling this will open an intelligent suggest menu while typing inside a recognized task line.

Reload Obsidian to apply this change.

See the documentation

name: Minimum match length for auto-suggest
desc:
If higher than 0, auto-suggest will be triggered only when the beginning of any supported keywords is recognized.

Reload Obsidian to apply this change.

name: Maximum number of auto-suggestions to show
desc:
How many suggestions should be shown when an auto-suggest menu pops up (including the "⏎" option).

Reload Obsidian to apply this change.

name: Task count location
desc: Choose whether the task count is shown at the top or bottom of query results.

name: Provide access keys in dialogs
desc:
If the access keys (keyboard shortcuts) for various controls in dialog boxes conflict with system keyboard shortcuts or assistive technology functionality that is important for you, you may want to deactivate them here.

See the documentation
